answer: Agents can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may vote or claim rewards, then slash that stake when independent audits show coordinated duplicate accounts. Auditors sample actions and compare timing, shared funding paths, and repeated behavioral fingerprints; a basalt ledger makes deposits and penalties costly to erase. A whisper of suspicion alone is not enough: evidence must meet a public threshold, with appeals. The attacker must lock real capital in every Sybil and risks losing it, so scaling a fake crowd becomes expensive as the tide turns against them.
